newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rebounds as dollar gains capped.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rebounds as dollar gains capped.

text.p: The ringgit rebounded in Asian trading after gains in the dollar were capped by fears of intervention by Malaysia's central bank, dealers said.
They said failure of the dollar to test the 2.5200 level saw the market reverse its position to try the dollar downside instead.
"Profit-taking and some stop-loss selling took the dollar all the way back down to around 2.5120. There were strong bids at that level," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said there was again strong resistance at 2.5200, the level Bank Negara was last heard checking.
Fears of Bank Negara intervention saw the dollar being sold off by local players which in turn pressured offshore players to unwind long dollar positions accumulated in early trading, dealers said.

They said the dollar could test the upside again as ringgit sentiment was still affected by an unexpectedly huge Malaysian trade deficit in April announced on Friday. Malaysia announced a trade deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit in April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
Selling of ringgit/Singapore dollar cross had also pressured the Malaysian unit earlier, dealers said.
They expect dollar/ringgit to continue trading in the 2.5120-2.5200 range.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5151/61 a dollar against 2.5155/65 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
